title: A `require` whose path is computed at run time compiles and runs nothing.
text: `string $path = "lib.nvs"; require $path;` compiles clean under `nvs run` and the statement does nothing: the file's statements do not run when it exists, nothing is thrown when it does not, and the value form `mixed $v = require $path;` gives `1`. `rule:statements/require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct` says a `require` throws when its target is missing, and `nvs_hir::requires`'s module doc leaves every path that is not literal text, class constants and `.` between them to a run-time resolve. No run-time resolve exists: `lower_expr_stmt`'s `ExprKind::Require` arm emits the call only where `require_target` recorded a file, and the matching arm in `crates/nvs-ir/src/lower/expr.rs` answers a tagged `1` otherwise. A program that loads a configuration file or an access check through a variable therefore carries on without it, and nothing says so. The file graph closes while compiling (`rule:programs/no-runtime-autoload`), so the fix is a decision before it is code: a path the walk cannot fold is refused where it is written, or the site throws at run time. Whether `nvs build --compile` already refuses such a path, as `rule:packaging/a-bundled-require-resolves-at-build-time` says it must, is not checked. `docs/reference/tools/30-php-differences.md` § *What parses but behaves differently* states only the written-path half, which `E0311` enforces and `tests/conformance/reject/a-missing-require-target-and-an-ordering-of-plain-objects-do-not-compile.nvst` pins.
